Ellama is an Emacs frontend for chatting with large language models via ~llm-ollama~.  Models run locally through Ollama – no cloud API needed.

- jdormit/emacs-opencode (https://github.com/jdormit/emacs-opencode) — native client: M-x opencode for sessions, opencode-ask for prompts, session management, and deep Emacs integration via emacs-mcp-server (read buffers, eval elisp, run compile commands)
- colobas/opencode.el (https://github.com/colobas/opencode.el) — port of my tools into gptel with LSP integration, diagnostics, symbol navigation, and agent presets
- rogs/opencode.el (https://git.rogs.me/rogs/opencode.el) — lightweight terminal-based integration using vterm or shell-mode with a transient menu
- xenodium/agent-shell (https://github.com/xenodium/agent-shell) — ACP-based native Emacs buffer for LLM agents, supports OpenCode as a backend
- tninja/ai-code-interface.el (https://github.com/tninja/ai-code-interface.el) — unified interface wrapping multiple CLI agents including OpenCode

No more hardcoded model list — when you pull a new model in Ollama, it appears in ~M-x ellama-switch-provider~ automatically
